namespace AbcAdaptation.Reference

/-!
# The Tate `q`-parameter

This file introduces the *Tate parameter* attached to a Tate elliptic curve: an element
`q` of the base field with `0 < ‖q‖ < 1`, together with its normalized additive order.

Over a complete nonarchimedean field `K`, a Tate curve is uniformized by the analytic
quotient `K̄ˣ / qᶻ`, and the multiplicative group generated by `q` is discrete precisely
because `0 < ‖q‖ < 1`. This module isolates the purely metric core of that datum, which
needs neither the nonarchimedean (ultrametric) hypothesis nor completeness: those enter in
the later files that build the `qᶻ`-action, the analytic quotient and the uniformization.

## Main definitions

* `TateCurvesTheta.TateParameter K`: an element `q : Kˣ` with `‖q‖ < 1`.
* `TateCurvesTheta.TateParameter.ord`: the normalized additive order `-Real.log ‖q‖`, a
  strictly positive real. This is the local-height/order convention of a Tate parameter
  (IUT I, Definition 3.1(c)); the integer/discrete normalization coming from a normalized
  valuation is deferred to the shared valuation infrastructure and refines this real order.

## Main results

* `TateParameter.ord_pos`: `0 < ord q`.
* `TateParameter.pow_ne_one`: `q` is not a root of unity (`qⁿ ≠ 1` for `n > 0`).
* `TateParameter.tendsto_pow_atTop_zero`: `qⁿ → 0`, so the positive powers of `q`
  accumulate only at `0`.

## References

* J. Tate, *A review of non-Archimedean elliptic functions*.
* J. H. Silverman, *Advanced Topics in the Arithmetic of Elliptic Curves*, Chapter V.
* S. Mochizuki, *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory I*, Definition 3.1(c).
-/

open Filter Topology

namespace TateCurvesTheta

variable (K : Type*) [NormedField K]

/-- A **Tate parameter** over a normed field `K`: a unit `q` with `‖q‖ < 1`.

The positivity `0 < ‖q‖` is automatic (`q` is a unit, hence nonzero), so the only genuine
field is the strict upper bound `‖q‖ < 1`. Over a complete nonarchimedean field this is the
datum from which the Tate curve `E_q` and its `q`-uniformization are built. -/
structure TateParameter where
  /-- The underlying unit of the base field. -/
  q : Kˣ
  /-- The Tate parameter has absolute value strictly less than one. -/
  norm_lt_one : ‖(q : K)‖ < 1

namespace TateParameter

variable {K}

variable (t : TateParameter K)

/-- The norm of a Tate parameter is strictly positive. -/
lemma norm_q_pos : 0 < ‖(t.q : K)‖ :=
  norm_pos_iff.mpr t.q.ne_zero

end TateParameter

end TateCurvesTheta

end AbcAdaptation.Reference
payload.natural_language_statement:
**Formal-code readback**

**English**

For a type K in an arbitrary universe with a NormedField instance, TateParameter(K) is the type of records with two fields: q is an element of the unit group K×, and norm_lt_one is a proof that the real number ‖(q:K)‖ is strictly less than 1. The constructor takes exactly such a unit and such an inequality proof; the projections return the unit and the inequality. A unit carries a multiplicative inverse, so its underlying field element is nonzero. Equivalently, the mathematical data are a nonzero element of K with norm less than 1; zero and elements of norm exactly 1 are excluded. No parameter is selected canonically and no existence or uniqueness of a record for a general K is asserted by this definition.

For every such K and every t:TateParameter(K), the lemma TateParameter.norm_q_pos asserts 0<‖(t.q:K)‖. Together with the record's inequality this places its norm strictly between 0 and 1. The assumptions consist only of the normed-field structure on K and the supplied record t; neither completeness, a non-Archimedean norm, discrete valuation, local compactness, nor a characteristic condition is required. In particular, if every nonzero element of K has norm at least 1, this record type has no elements; the lemma is still a universal conditional statement about any supplied t. No curve, period quotient, or further geometric object is part of the formal declarations in this packet.

**简体中文**

设 K 是任意宇宙中的类型，并带有赋范域结构。TateParameter(K) 是具有两个字段的记录类型：q 是单位群 K× 的元素，norm_lt_one 是实数不等式 ‖(q:K)‖<1 的证明。构造子恰好接收这样一个单位及该不等式的证明；两个投影分别返回单位与不等式。单位带有乘法逆元，因此其对应的域元素非零。等价地，这里的数学数据是 K 中范数小于 1 的一个非零元素；零元和范数恰为 1 的元素都被排除。定义没有选定规范的参数，也没有断言一般的 K 中存在或唯一存在这样的记录。

对于每个这样的 K 以及每个 t:TateParameter(K)，引理 TateParameter.norm_q_pos 断言 0<‖(t.q:K)‖。结合记录中的不等式，其范数严格位于 0 与 1 之间。假设只有 K 的赋范域结构和所给记录 t；不要求完备性、非 Archimedes 范数、离散赋值、局部紧致性或任何特征条件。特别地，若 K 的每个非零元素的范数都至少为 1，则该记录类型没有元素；引理仍然是关于任何给定 t 的全称条件陈述。此代码包的形式声明不包含曲线、周期商或其他几何对象。

**日本語**

任意の宇宙に属する型 K にノルム体の構造を与える。TateParameter(K) は二つのフィールドを持つレコードの型である。q は単数群 K× の元であり、norm_lt_one は実数の不等式 ‖(q:K)‖<1 の証明である。構成子はそのような単数と不等式の証明をちょうど受け取り、二つの射影は単数および不等式を返す。単数は乗法逆元を持つため、その基礎となる体の元は非零である。同値な数学的データは、ノルムが 1 未満である K の非零元である。零元およびノルムがちょうど 1 の元は除外される。この定義は標準的なパラメータを選ばず、一般の K におけるレコードの存在や一意存在も主張しない。

各 K および各 t:TateParameter(K) に対し、補題 TateParameter.norm_q_pos は 0<‖(t.q:K)‖ を述べる。レコードの不等式と合わせると、そのノルムは 0 と 1 の間に厳密に入る。仮定は K のノルム体構造と与えられたレコード t だけであり、完備性、非アルキメデス的ノルム、離散付値、局所コンパクト性、標数に関する条件は要求されない。特に K の各非零元のノルムが 1 以上なら、このレコード型は空である。それでも補題は、与えられた任意の t に関する全称的な条件文である。このコード群の形式的宣言には、曲線、周期による商、その他の幾何学的対象は含まれない。

**Paper source context (English; separate from the formal-code readback)**

**Paper source context.** Mochizuki I, Definition 3.1(c) (p. 62), imposes a coprimality condition on the orders of the elliptic curve’s $q$-parameters and explicitly calls them local heights by reference to *Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position*, Definition 3.3. In that original paper, §3 first fixes a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ with a surjective discrete valuation and a split multiplicative-reduction elliptic-curve model (pp. 14–15); Definition 3.3 calls the positive integer $v_K(q_E)$ its local height. This is the curve-associated arithmetic setting served by the much smaller selected metric carrier.

**Implementation scope.** The selected commands are only TateParameter and norm_q_pos. For any normed field $K$, TateParameter consists of a unit $q\in K^{\times}$ and the strict inequality $\lVert q\rVert<1$. norm_q_pos proves $0<\lVert q\rVert$ from invertibility in the field. Neither completeness nor an ultrametric norm is assumed. The carrier does not include an elliptic curve, a discrete valuation, a normalized local height, or a Tate uniformization. Thus a member of this generic type is not by definition the paper’s curve-associated parameter. The source file’s real-valued order, convergence, and non-torsion lemmas are not selected outputs. No equality between a metric expression and the paper’s integer local height is asserted by this unit.

Shinichi Mochizuki, *Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory I: Construction of Hodge Theaters* (May 2020), Definition 3.1(c), second complete sentence; printed/PDF page(s) 62.

> Also, we suppose that $l$ is prime to the [residue characteristics of the] elements of $\mathbb V_{\mathrm{mod}}^{\mathrm{bad}}$, as well as to the orders of the $q$-parameters of $E_F$ [i.e., in the terminology of [GenEll], Definition 3.3, the “local heights” of $E_F$] at the primes of $\mathbb V(F)^{\mathrm{bad}}$.

Shinichi Mochizuki, *Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position* (February 2009), §3, paragraph introducing local theory at nonarchimedean primes, immediately before the torsion discussion; printed/PDF page(s) 14, 15.

> Next, we consider the local theory at nonarchimedean primes. Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ [where $p$ is a prime number] with residue field $k$, maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_K\subseteq\mathcal O_K$, and valuation map $v_K:K^{\times}\to\mathbb Z$ [which we normalize so that $v_K$ is surjective]; $\overline K$ an algebraic closure of $K$; $G_K\overset{\mathrm{def}}{=}\operatorname{Gal}(\overline K/K)$; $E\to\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_K)$ a one-dimensional semi-abelian scheme over $\mathcal O_K$ such that the generic fiber $E_K$ of $E$ is proper, while the special fiber $E_k$ of $E$ is isomorphic to $(\mathbb G_m)_k$, the multiplicative group over $k$.

Shinichi Mochizuki, *Arithmetic Elliptic Curves in General Position* (February 2009), Definition 3.3, complete definition; printed/PDF page(s) 15.

> We shall refer to the positive integer $v_K(q_E)\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ as the local height of $E$ [or $E_K$].

**Actual consumer.** The graph records TateParameter→AdmissiblePrimeData→theorem110. Its positivity lemma feeds orderZ_pos and toOrdered, then qOrder and logQAt before theorem110. The later normalized-order infrastructure supplies the additional valuation data; the two selected commands do not construct that bridge.

These Definitions are detached source preparation; the consumer paths describe the original reference graph and do not establish live mission-root membership or S2-04 completion.
